description: Recertifying Utility Workers in a Small, Remote Community is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by American Samoa Power Authority; University of Hawai'i Sea Grant. The American Samoa Power Authority (ASPA), a Samoan government-owned water, wastewater, and power utility, faces many challenges in bolstering its workforce, including population decline, limited access to technical resources, aging and poorly mapped utility systems, limited financial resources, limited opportunities for worker advancement, and exposure to disruptive climate-related hazards. Coverage: American Samoa (2024). The toolkit gives American Samoa as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
